answer: Each identity opens a signal thread on the river ledger: five chained receipts, each bound to its key and thread position. A thread locks a 50-credit bond. Auditors recompute the signal against the river ledger; a reused receipt, wrong key, or broken link burns the bond. Each receipt costs 12 credits, so one fake costs 110, and the k-th fake pays 110 because receipts cannot move to another thread. A thousand fakes cost 110,000 credits and need 5,000 receipts. A rented thread ring fails: a rented receipt carries another key or wrong position. An honest agent opens one thread, paying 110 once.
